direct_public_P_lane_additions.name: MATCHED_CNF
direct_public_P_lane_additions.admission: Incidence bipartite graph has a matching covering every clause.
direct_public_P_lane_additions.solve: A matching gives each clause a distinct representative variable; set each representative to satisfy its matched clause.
direct_public_P_lane_additions.limitation: Membership implies SAT; this is not an UNSAT class.
references: Franco and Van Gelder, A perspective on certain polynomial-time solvable classes of satisfiability, Discrete Applied Mathematics 125 (2003).
Szeider, Matched Formulas and Backdoor Sets.

direct_public_P_lane_additions.name: HITTING_CNF
direct_public_P_lane_additions.admission: Every pair of clauses clashes on complementary literals.
direct_public_P_lane_additions.solve: SAT/model count is polynomial; falsifying assignment sets of clauses are disjoint, yielding direct counting and decision.
references: Iwama, CNF-Satisfiability Test by Counting and Polynomial Average Time, 1989.
Peitl and Szeider, Are hitting formulas hard for resolution?, Discrete Applied Mathematics 337 (2023).

direct_public_P_lane_additions.name: CC_BALANCED_CNF
references: Balanced / CC-balanced SAT literature summarized by Franco and Van Gelder 2003.

direct_public_P_lane_additions.name: LINEARLY_SATISFIABLE_CNF
direct_public_P_lane_additions.admission: Canonical polynomial linear-autarky decomposition has empty linearly-lean remainder.
direct_public_P_lane_additions.recognition: Largest linear autark part / linearly lean remainder is computable in polynomial time by linear programming.
direct_public_P_lane_additions.solve: A linear autarky satisfying the full clause-set provides a SAT certificate; unassigned variables may be completed arbitrarily.
direct_public_P_lane_additions.relationship: Strictly useful as a wider SAT-only door; literature states it generalizes matched formulas and contains satisfiable q-Horn formulas modulo unit-clause elimination.
references: Oliver Kullmann, Investigations on autark assignments, Discrete Applied Mathematics 107 (2000/2001).

parameterized_lane_additions.name: MAXIMUM_DEFICIENCY
parameterized_lane_additions.parameter: k = md(F), maximum clause-variable deficiency over all subformulas.
parameterized_lane_additions.parameter_discovery: Polynomial via bipartite maximum matching / Hall deficiency.
parameterized_lane_additions.polynomial_coverage_condition: k=O(log n), or fixed constant k.
parameterized_lane_additions.importance: Orthogonal to treewidth: known families have bounded md and unbounded treewidth, and vice versa.
references: Stefan Szeider, Minimal unsatisfiable formulas with bounded clause-variable difference are fixed-parameter tractable, JCSS 69 (2004).

parameterized_lane_additions.name: DELETION_DISTANCE_TO_Q_HORN
parameterized_lane_additions.parameter: minimum deletion q-Horn backdoor size k
parameterized_lane_additions.result: SAT is fixed-parameter tractable in this distance; q-Horn strictly contains Horn, Krom and renamable Horn.
parameterized_lane_additions.polynomial_promotion_rule: Do not infer k=O(log n) => polynomial until the imported implementation's explicit parameter dependence is frozen and shown polynomial under the proposed bound.
references: Gaspers, Ordyniak, Ramanujan, Saurabh, Szeider, Backdoors to q-Horn, STACS 2013 / Algorithmica.

parameterized_lane_additions.name: BACKDOOR_DEPTH_TO_SCHAEFER
parameterized_lane_additions.result: Backdoor depth admits FPT approximation; CNF-SAT is linear-time for bounded depth.
parameterized_lane_additions.significance: Depth can stay constant while ordinary backdoor size is arbitrarily large, so it is a genuinely different funnel door.
parameterized_lane_additions.polynomial_promotion_rule: Bounded constant depth is direct polynomial coverage. Any growing-depth claim requires the explicit approximation/solve dependence before promotion.
references: Dreier, Ordyniak, Szeider, SAT backdoors: Depth beats size, JCSS 142 (2024).

parameterized_lane_additions.name: HETEROGENEOUS_SCHAEFER_BACKDOOR
parameterized_lane_additions.result: Strong backdoor detection to heterogeneous unions/combinations of Schaefer tractable classes has an established parameterized complexity landscape with FPT cases and single-exponential improvements.
parameterized_lane_additions.value: Different assignments to one backdoor may land in different known P classes, potentially shrinking the required set versus one homogeneous target.
references: Gaspers, Misra, Ordyniak, Szeider, Zivny, Backdoors into Heterogeneous Classes of SAT and CSP, AAAI 2014 / JCSS 85 (2017).
parameterized_lane_additions.firewall: Use only exact theorem-supported combinations; do not treat arbitrary union of tractable classes as tractable.

negative_public_guidance.reason: SAT parameterized by undirected clique-width of the incidence graph is W[1]-hard in the known result.
negative_public_guidance.reference: Ordyniak, Paulusma, Szeider, Satisfiability of acyclic and almost acyclic CNF formulas, TCS 481 (2013).

negative_public_guidance.reason: SAT algorithms exist for extended Horn, but polynomial recognition of the full extended-Horn class is not known in the cited literature; simple extended/enlarged Horn subclasses have recognizers.
SAT can be efficiently solved when the SLUR algorithm succeeds, but membership testing in SLUR is coNP-complete.

universal_funnel_refinement.theorem_target: For every reachable residual, a uniform polynomial procedure must either enter a direct P lane, certify a parameter bound that makes an imported parameterized solver polynomial, or perform an exact globally polynomially charged transition that moves toward such a door.
